_about: Enemies inside a skirmish: the domains' wildlife and the heroes (bible section 9; the names are working names until play moves them, the numbers placeholders at the single-digit scale since the stock pass's landing (22 October): HP 2 to 6 for the rank and file, 30 to 40 massive, 12 to 24 heroes, the slate's bosses 48 at tier one (30 October, on the kill-time test's read, Ryan's word to keep what scales best; a core in parts 40, a part 8 to 12, the Vampire Lord 40 since it may rise once), a blow 1 to 6 and a boss's 6 to 10; docs/rules.md). hp is a foe's HP, the foes' word (a machine has hull). Enemy damage is static and telegraphed exactly; only the player's rolled faces roll. rank is where they prefer to stand: front foes step up, back foes hold. size 2 is massive and fills both slots of a column, at any tier. tier (1 to 3, one by default) is the rung of its line a unit stands on: a recolour is a base type in a new hue under a new name, its own foe type with its own numbers and a twist (the Goblin Guard and the Goblin Captain on the Goblin), carrying its tier; which units come is the domain's spawn list at the battle's tier (content/factions.json), a boss's escort included, so the field never reads this. elite true marks a foe that leads an elite composition (content/factions.json; the bible's tiers row: a guaranteed mini-boss event a Fracture spawns mid-battle, outside the spawn lists, scaled by the tier as a boss is since 2 November); its menace is doubled (ContentDB.menace: the heaviest implemented blow plus a quarter of HP, rounded up, the one weight for the Rupture meter, Anathema and salvage). wanders true marks the elite any domain's Fracture may send: drawn by chance (ContentDB.WANDER_CHANCE) in place of the domain's next own elite, always once its own are spent; an elite may come again in a later battle, never twice in one. hero marks one of the party: human-sized, the domain's final, dealt from the domain's bench at the campaign's start; a hero is never in a spawn list. promotes names the hero a massive entry is the class change of, its promoted form fought at the finale (bible section 9): the entry holds what the class change adds (size 2, rank front, its armour, its one move more under actions, a move with one of the hero's ids taking that move's place) and everything else, its name included, is its hero's, read as the content loads. armour (default 0) comes off every blow that lands on the foe, flat, never off Burning, Vitriol or a breaching weapon. No foe resists a suppress by nature: Numbed, from a suppress that lands, is the only resistance. aim is the sense a foe's target pick follows, each foe on its own as the round opens: anything (the default, at random, the baseline the numbers are balanced on), and where a foe's threat calls for one, exposed (weighted toward the machine its blows would hurt most), heat (the hottest machine), armed (a machine showing an intact weapon), focus (the rank shares one pick), buffed (the machine carrying the most stacks). A move may carry its own aim. The foes pick in the order they strike and never over-commit: a machine the blows already picked would wreck is passed over while another stands. on_death {summon, count, pair}: destroyed, the foe splits, that many of the named foe stepping up at once under its pack, the first into the slot it fell from and the rest into the nearest empty slots of their rank, any with no room into the pool; with pair (the Gel, count 2) both halves stand as a pair in its own slot, one slot to the formation (an area blow reaching both, a single-target blow one, no mine laid there while either stands); an arrival's round is over (no intent, acting from the next round), and a split goes one deep; on_death {blow} is a last act, landed the moment it falls. parts, guard and regrow_parts make a core in parts. Player-facing text: codex (what the codex says), flavour (an in-world quote), and each action's text. Every move wears the genre's name where the genre has one (Protect, Cure, Fire, Steal, Self-Destruct) while the engine's words stay ours; the plaque announces a named move when it lands (bible section 9). design is internal and never shown: fantasy (the pitch, the source of the homage), niche (the tactical problem the foe poses), sprite and variants (the art's briefs), and notes only where something is still owed. actions is the foe's roster of moves, each kind attack, defend, buff or debuff, with status implemented or planned; only implemented actions appear in the codex, and a planned move may name an effect the engine lacks (flee, interpose, retaliate). Rank and file have one or two moves, a boss or a hero three, the third a signature that opens on a condition. A move may carry when, one word or a list meaning any (below_half, missing_hull, back_behind, others_on_field, ally_hurt, machine_buffed, ally_unready, ally_marked); a move whose condition fails is not rolled, and a special never fires twice running when anything else is open. A defend, buff or debuff names an effect the engine runs (Foe.ACTION_EFFECTS: brace with value (the armour it adds, in stacks of Armoured, a point a stack; brace_all the same on every foe through the next round), regrow with value, regrow_ally (the most hurt of its own); revive_once, revive_once_ally (Reraise on one of its own), summon with foe and count, rally with value; drain_rerolls, burn with value (stacks of Burning on its target), disable, scorch_all with value (stacks of Scorched on every machine), corrupt_all with value (stacks of Corrupted on the entry every machine shows), silence, dispel (Purge); cleanse (every mark the team laid off the most-marked of its own, no value), barrier (a Barrier on itself, no value), regenerate with value (Regenerating on itself), ward_all (a Ward on every foe on the field, no value), prime with value (Primed on every other foe)) and is picked by weight like an attack, in place of a blow that turn. Write {value} in its text for its number. On the map: zone is the pack's ring in hexes (default 1; a hunter's 2 at least, since it pounces), behaviour push (default; toward the gate) or hunt (one machine, locked at spawn and kept while it stands; hunts names the caveat: nearest, weakest, strongest, slowest, fastest; a prey sealed off by walls and machines costs the machine nearest it that the hunter can reach that turn), movespeed in hexes (default 2; foes wade water at two a hex as ground machines do and walls stop them, and a winged foe (winged true) crosses both as a flyer does; bosses patrol 1). An implemented attack scales the base attack: factor (default 1.0), strikes (default 1; each a separate blow), swarm (so much more per other foe of its type on the field), countdown (it gathers that many rounds and lands later), keywords (breach: the blow ignores the shield and the armour, the whole of it reaching the hull; scorch: stacks of Scorched; burn: stacks of Burning; disable and corrupt act on the entry the machine's die shows; scorch, burn and corrupt each say their stacks a blow beside the keyword, as the player's Burn does ("scorch": 2); self_destruct: the blow spends the striker; all: the blow lands on every machine), weight (default 1; attacks weigh 2 to a special's 1). Write {damage} in an action's text and the resulting number is shown. Foes stand and strike front rank left to right then back rank; the heaviest hitters deploy left.

entries.codex: The Meadow's rank and file. Small, loud and never alone: they come in sixes, straight at the nearest thing with a heartbeat, and the more of them stand the harder each one hits.

actions.text: A beak like a pick, for {damage}; the component the machine is showing bites when spent.

design.fantasy: The dead in rusted ornate plate: a knight's silhouette gone wrong, the helm empty, the plate hanging off the ribs. The genre's zombies and skeletons in one.
design.niche: There are six of them and four slots. Kill fast or be buried: every one standing makes every other one hit harder.

entries.codex: The rank and file of the Marsh. Slow, stupid and never alone: six arrive for every one you put down, and they walk straight at the nearest thing with a heartbeat. The more of them stand, the harder each one hits.

actions.name: Claw
actions.text: Tears at anything in reach for {damage}: more for every other revenant standing.

entries.flavour: They don't run. They don't have to. You'll get tired first.

entries.name: Wight

design.fantasy: The wight, the Marsh's hard-to-keep-down on the rank and file: Regenerating as a foe's buff. Tier two of the revenant line.

entries.codex: A revenant that knits itself back together. Hurt, it regrows a little at each action for three rounds: burst it, or purge the mending.

actions.name: Claw
actions.text: Tears at anything in reach for {damage}: more for every other wight standing.

actions.name: Grave Mend
actions.text: Knits itself: regrows {value} at each of its next three actions.

entries.flavour: You can hear it mending. Finish it before it finishes.

entries.name: Lich

design.fantasy: The lich, the Marsh's commander. Tier three of the revenant line. Its Dark Rite, a delayed heal on a countdown, is planned until the engine has a special with a countdown (Ryan, 28 October, mentioned a delayed heal; not built here).

entries.codex: The dead that commands the dead. It readies an ally to get back up once, and strikes from the back. Reach it, or purge what it readies.

actions.name: Reraise
actions.text: Readies one of its own, never itself: the next time it falls it gets back up, whole, once.

actions.name: Dark Rite

entries.flavour: It does not fight. It makes sure the others do not stop.

design.niche: It hides behind the wall and keeps the wall standing. Reach it, or chew through.

entries.codex: Keeps to the back rank behind a wall of the dead and keeps the wall standing. Anything that can reach past the front is worth more here than anywhere else.

entries.name: Spectre

entries.name: Wraith

entries.flavour: Three jobs, one ghost. Reach it.

design.fantasy: The genre's death knight: a cape, rusted plate, a sword as long as it is tall.

entries.name: Barrow Giant

actions.text: Ribs fly: {damage} to every machine.

entries.name: Goblin Shaman

design.fantasy: The warband's commander, the goblin that protects his allies (Ryan, 15 October: a decent elite; the marked goblin_takesD_1). The tier-one elite: a harder fight that hits harder while it stands, so reach the back first.

design.notes: Proposed 26 October; landed 30 October as a placeholder kit for Ryan's marks. No art yet: the views' placeholder shape until a recolour or a pick is cut.

entries.name: Floraison

design.fantasy: Clair Obscur's Bourgeon by archetype, under Ryan's name (15 October: the flowering): a humanoid plant whose head is a flower's maw. The game places one in its Meadows. Art picked 26 October (the paint-out of the maw's eyes).
design.niche: It takes a machine out of the fight: the swallow holds one machine for two rounds, until Floraison falls or until it has lost a quarter of its HP since, so the team fights a man down, answered before it lands by a Ward, a Lure, a Suppress or a Disrupt and after it by focus on Floraison. Its combos are many small strikes, which plate shrugs off: lure them onto the tank.

The release at a quarter of its HP lost since the swallow, Ryan's 31 October (agreeing Claude's lean on his Clair Obscur stagger); a lost action on top, the stagger's bigger form, waits on the plain release reading weak.

entries.name: Gilgamesh

design.fantasy: Final Fantasy's recurring rival and weapon collector; Gilgamesh is a myth's name, so it stays (the names rule). On the slate by Claude's lean, then an elite that can turn up in any domain (Ryan, 24 October: tempted to move him to the elites, "since he can pop up anywhere"; 31 October, agreed).
design.niche: He takes what a machine is showing and swings it back next round at its own number: a weapon's blow, or a fake for 1 if he took a shield, a vent, equipment or a blank. What shows on the die he picks is the player's to choose.
design.notes: Landed 30 October as a boss, a runnable placeholder kit for Ryan's marks; an elite since 31 October, the one that wanders (Ryan: "I agree with everything", of Claude's lean): Final Fantasy V banished him into the rift between worlds, and he turns up uninvited in other worlds ever since, so he walks out of any rift, drawn by chance at any domain's Fracture in place of its next own elite and always once its own are spent (2 November), and the one elite scaled by the tier as a boss is, since he may come at any tier. At an elite's 40 HP. Every number a placeholder. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked.

entries.name: The Fallen Weapon

design.fantasy: The Exor homage (Super Mario RPG's sword fallen into the keep; a series coinage, so a name of ours, the Fallen Weapon a working name). Ryan, 15 October: in, distinct from its game's look; 18 October, his pick: the double-bitted axe standing haft-down, an eye in each blade. The boss in parts: the eyes shield the core that drives them.
design.niche: Its core is Guarded while both eyes stand: one eye down opens it for three rounds before the eye grows back. One eye's stare goes through the shield, the other's switches off what a machine shows, the Waste's two halves. Below half it rises and falls on every machine two rounds on.
design.notes: Landed 30 October as a runnable placeholder kit for Ryan's marks (the slate, docs/bosses_proposal.md); every number a placeholder. The eyes are foes of their own with no art yet (the placeholder shape); the core is drawn as the whole axe, its blades and their eyes included, until the eyes are cut apart or rendered.

entries.name: Cinder Tortoise

entries.name: The Djinn

design.fantasy: The desert's own spirit, the genie by archetype (the jinn are the Thousand and One Nights' and older, a myth's word, so it stays). The Waste's third boss for a day (31 October), then the rank and file (Ryan, 2 November: "Djinn can be a rank-and-file since its a trope archetype. Could be backline, frontline, or massive, depending on the slant"); Claude's slant the back-rank caster, the Waste's first purge in the ranks (section 12's carrier question), since the slate's kit was built to carry it.
design.niche: The Waste's purge in the ranks: it unmakes what a machine's die bought, every buff a face granted, on the machine carrying the most, and hurt it slips into a mirage, a Barrier that eats the next weapon blow. A back-rank caster: reach it, spend a buff before it is unmade, or put the buff on the machine it is not aiming at.

entries.name: The Ruby Colossus

design.fantasy: Final Fantasy VII's Ruby Weapon by archetype (WEAPON is the series' coinage, so a name of ours; the Ruby Colossus a working name): the red colossus buried in the desert round the Gold Saucer, its tentacles in the sand, whose Whirlsand blew a party member out of the fight. The Waste's third boss since 2 November (Ryan: "Ruby weapon is cool"), in the Djinn's place.
design.niche: A boss in parts with no guard: its two tentacles hit on their own, one through the shield and one twice, and grow back three rounds after they fall, so every die is a choice between the arms and the body. Whirlsand buries a machine (a swallow: two rounds, until the Colossus falls, or until it has lost a quarter of its HP since). Below half, Ultima gathers for three rounds and lands on every machine. Dig the machine out by focus on the body, kill the breaching arm or eat its blows, and shield everything for Ultima.
design.notes: Landed 2 November as a runnable placeholder kit for Ryan's marks; every number a placeholder. Its tentacles' blows of 6 and 4 and a regrowth of two rounds walled the stock teams alone at tiers two and three (docs/measurements.md, 2 November): 4, 3 and three rounds since, on the what-if. Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked. Its escort a Basilisk and a Pit Antlion at tier two, Gorgons, the Antlion Queen and a Pit Antlion at tier three: stone and pits beside a buried machine, so the tempo it takes is pressed.

entries.name: The Vampire Lord

design.niche: Hard to keep down, the Marsh's own: its bite heals what it takes from the hull, it readies itself once a fight to get back up whole, and below half it drinks from every machine. Shield what it bites (a shield starves the drain), burn it (Burning takes back what it drains), stop the readying (a Suppress, a Disrupt, a Purge on its Getting Back Up), and burst it twice if it rises.

Its art a rough placeholder (tools/placeholder_art.py), a reminder until a render is picked. At 40 HP, under the slate's 48, since it may rise once whole. Its drain takes from the hull alone: one of shield and hull walled Wainwright & Sutler's trio at every HP tried down to 24 (0 to 10% won), the shield doing nothing against the heal; hull only, every row won it at 40 (30 October, docs/measurements.md).

design.fantasy: Clair Obscur's Sciel by archetype (Ryan, 16 October): the reader of fate who marks a foe and collects later, her twin-bladed scythe her defining feature (a staff with a reaping blade at each end, spun and thrown). Ryan's name, 16 October: the Augur read omens for Rome. Her look is ours: a laced leather vest, shirt, trousers and boots, bare-headed, the bone charms, the long crescent blades (Ryan's notes of 18 October over three rounds, each asking for less cloth and bigger blades; the hero style prompt's robes and flowing cloth, and this text's own words for what she must not wear, were what kept drawing them, so her renders take a prompt of their own that names only what she wears).
design.niche: The Marsh's back rank, in the Necromancer's place (dumped 16 October, the weakest homage). Her omen is the countdown: named at one machine as the round opens, it lands two rounds on, so the warning is the whole fight (shield that machine, Suppress or Disrupt her, or reach her first). Below half every omen comes due at once, on every machine, the next round: the countdown and the every-machine blow on one move.
design.notes: Working names (Reap, Omen, Harvest). The twin scythe matters in the art (Ryan): both blades must read in every take.

entries.codex: A reader of omens at the back. She names a machine and its doom lands two rounds on, so the warning is the whole fight: shield it, hold her, or reach her first. Hurt, she calls every omen due at once, on everyone.

design.fantasy: The one who calls something bigger: Final Fantasy's summoner, Golden Sun's adepts, the demon summoners of Megami Tensei. Its summons answer the deep violet circle, appear for one move, and go. Its own power shows as deep violet rune circles in its palms, never fire (the Black Mage's) and never the rock (the Elemental's): Ryan, 13 October; the fire and the ice are the summons'.
design.niche: On its own it is a mage with a weak blow; its summons are the fight, each a move rather than a companion (three massive companions could not stand in two ranks of four, and the Tamer and the Necromancer already call foes into the fight every round). Skaði's frost corrupts the component every machine shows; Surtr's fire scorches every machine once it is hurt. The answer is the back rank: reach it, Suppress it or Disrupt it.

entries.codex: A small figure in the back rank whose circle calls what answers it: Skaði, whose frost bites the component every machine shows, and once it is hurt, Surtr, whose fire scorches the whole field. Reach the back rank before the circle opens.
